articles.title: Swing-and-a-miss: MLB rescinds idea to host baseball game in national park after backlash
articles.summary: Officials in Wyoming had called notion to host game in Grand Teton national park ‘deeply unwelcome’ Major League Baseball (MLB) leadership is no longer considering holding a game inside a national park, according to a letter commissioner Robert Manfred sent to officials in Teton county, Wyoming, on…
body: On 26 September, the Washington Post reported that MLB had reached out to the White House about staging a one-day game at Grand Teton national park in Wyoming. Teton county describes itself as a “a year-round resort community” and sits within the Jackson Hole valley. It’s also a habitat for grizzly bears, osprey, bison and more.

News of MLB’s outreach to the federal government quickly sparked concern about the impact that erecting a field and the infrastructure to hold spectators could have on the natural landscape and habitat of scores of wildlife that call the 310,000-acre (125,500-hectare) park home.

In the letter, Manfred noted that MLB had held games at places like the Fort Bragg military base in North Carolina and the nation’s oldest Negro Leagues stadium in Birmingham, Alabama. He added that MLB staff had been doing their due diligence to see whether a game at Grand Teton was possible and to evaluate the potential environmental impact.
“Since the story was reported, it has become clear that the local community does not want us to continue Grand Teton national park as a potential site,” Manfred wrote.

articles.title: Bellamy says Wales 'stick' hurt as Norway win lifts mood
articles.summary: Head coach Craig Bellamy says he has been through a "really difficult" spell because of criticism aimed in his direction during Wales' winless run.
body: Bellamy's Wales claimed the finest result of his reign as they came from behind to beat Norway 2-1 at the Cardiff City Stadium on Thursday.
The victory ended a six-game winless run which began with defeat by Bosnia-Herzegovina in the World Cup play-off semi-final in March.
When asked whether Wales' success had lifted a weight off his shoulders, Bellamy revealed he had "felt the stick" ever since the Bosnia loss.
"But I've seen it; I've drawn on experience because I've seen managers before me get it.

articles.title: Pro-Palestine protests interrupt game as Ireland pass up 2-0 lead in draw against Austria
articles.summary: Protests halted events in Dublin twice before the Republic of Ireland were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw after Austria came back in the second half of their Nations League encounter at the Aviva Stadium.
body: Despite a significant security presence, the contest was twice interrupted in the opening 45 minutes, first due to what campaign group Stop the Game later referred to in a statement as a “limited tennis ball protest”, when – around the 20th minute – tennis balls wrapped in stickers featuring the Palestinian flag and the text “#StopTheGame” were launched on the pitch.
Then around the 35th minute a man ran on to the field of play from the opposite side carrying what appeared to be a Palestinian flag and was immediately tackled by security and carried off.

It has been a tumultuous week for the Republic. Their two Nations League fixtures against Israel have divided opinion in the country, sparking protests, including one which took place pre-match outside the stadium. The Republic’s behind-closed-doors “home” game against Israel in Backa Topola, Serbia, is scheduled for Sunday, and the manager Heimir Hallgrímsson on Wednesday confirmed it was their intention to play.
Troy Parrott got the hosts under way with a sensational 12th-minute opener and added a penalty on the stroke of half-time.

articles.summary: Spurs star says he will ‘never’ promote betting. Wembanyama says endorsements must reflect his values. James, Durant and Antetokounmpo have gambling ties. Victor Wembanyama has ruled out ever endorsing a sports betting company, saying he was saddened to see fellow NBA players lend their names to…
body: The San Antonio Spurs star was unequivocal when asked after Thursday’s training camp workout if he would consider partnering with a sportsbook.
“Absolutely not,” Wembanyama said. “I will never do that. Honestly, I think it’s very sad to see some players promote it. Everybody does whatever they want, but without me.”

Wembanyama said his approach to sponsorships has evolved during his ascent to one of basketball’s biggest stars. While money once factored into his thinking, he said he has come to prioritize whether potential partnerships align with his personal values.
“In the past, there was a dimension of money,” he said. “Not anymore.”

articles.title: Why Burnham's about-turn on Manchester City matters
articles.summary: The prime minister's comments on Man City were revealing on several levels - and leapt on by many in football, the BBC's political editor writes.
body: The rows circulating around Manchester City are huge, and they are only going to get bigger.
The Premier League has concluded that City "systematically broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade".
This, clearly, matters for the club, but that is just the start of it.

It matters for Manchester, it matters for the Premier League and so, crucially, it matters for the UK's image around the world – because England's top flight is a colossal global brand. In other words, this matters whether you like football or not.

articles.title: Real submit 'substantial' dossier in Barca payments case
articles.summary: Real Madrid have sent Uefa "evidence of extraordinary gravity" relating to payments made by Barcelona to a former vice-president of Spain's referees' committee.
body: European football's governing body says it will assess the documents - linked to allegations of 8.4m euros (£7.2m) being paid by Barcelona to Jose Maria Enriquez Negreira between 2001 and 2018 - as part of their ongoing review of the case.

Barcelona have repeatedly denied any wrongdoing since the matter came to light in 2023, stressing that the money paid was for scouting and technical reports provided by Negreira and his Dasnil 95 company about officials.

However, Real say that their new dossier, which is reported to be more than 50,000 pages in length, details contains evidence "which directly affects the integrity of the competition and confidence in the refereeing system".
Uefa described the dossier as "substantial" and said its ethics and disciplinary inspectors will "assess it as part of their ongoing review".

articles.title: What Went Wrong for the Astros in Wild Card Loss
articles.summary: The Houston Astros' postseason is over after being swept by the Chicago White Sox in the American League Wild Card Series. Houston dropped Game 1 by a score of 6-3 before falling 7-3 in Game 2, ending its postseason hopes after just two games. What went wrong?
body: Astros ace Hunter Brown was supposed to be the guy who saved the team. After Houston dropped game one, the Astros had their ace on the mound with the season on the line. Brown finished the regular season with a 3.19 ERA and had dominated the White Sox earlier in the season, allowing no runs over seven innings in a July matchup. Instead, Brown couldn’t even make it out of the first inning.

The White Sox sent nine batters to the plate against him and scored four runs before manager Joe Espada had to make the call to the bullpen. Brown gave up five hits, walked one, and was charged with four runs, three of them earned, while throwing 36 pitches. The defense certainly didn’t help him, but Brown was supposed to be the Astros’ ace, and he needed to find a way to limit the damage. He didn’t.

articles.title: Reviewing the Bears’ PFN grades from Week 3 vs. Eagles
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears bounced back in a major way on Monday night, picking up the decisive 27-7 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles to improve to 2-1 for the season. It was about as thorough a beating as one could imagine.
body: Each week, I’ll review how Chicago’s eligible performers graded by Pro Football Network’s Impact Scoring model. Here’s how Week 3 looked.

Week 3 marked the second week in a row that Darnell Wright finished with the highest PFN OL Impact grade of any offensive tackle in the NFL. He remains the top-graded lineman in the league, regardless of position. Keenum was quite efficient with his workload, ranking No. 12 in the NFL with 0.18 EPA per dropback. Though he finished the game with a strong 70.6% completion percentage, his completion percentage over expected (CPOE) was just +2.8. That generally suggests Ben Johnson did a good job making life easier with assignments to manage.

After a stellar outing in Week 3, Dillon Thieneman now ranks as the second-best safety in the NFL by PFN SAF Impact grading to start the year. Against Philadelphia, he allowed a targeted passer rating of just 2.8 in coverage, with his key interception of Andy Dalton in the end zone playing a major factor in the Bears’ win. Elsewhere in the secondary, Jaylon Johnson remains an analytical liability. However, both Devin Bush and T.J. Edwards have graded above average in coverage at the linebacker position.

articles.title: Shaw earns Man City draw with late Real goal dramatically disallowed
articles.summary: Bunny Shaw and a dramatic last-gasp decision from the referee ensured Manchester City took a point off Real Madrid with a 1-1 draw in the Women's Champions League.
body: Standout Linda Caicedo had given Real the lead in the first half but City improved after the interval and Shaw levelled with an equally expert finish across the goalkeeper to put the league-phase clash in the balance.
Shaw headed over and Yui Hasegawa volleyed wide for the hosts before Ayaka Yamashita had to pull off an excellent stop to deny Irune Dorado as both sides pushed for a winner.

Silvia Cristobal thought she had clinched it in the 89th minute for Real Madrid with a wonderful finish into the top corner - but referee Silvia Gasperotti had whistled to stop play after inadvertently blocking Beth Mead from reaching the ball.

Real Madrid's players and coaching staff were furious and appealed for the goal to stand but ultimately this closely fought contest ended in a draw - the same result City achieved in their opening game away to Bayern Munich last week.

articles.title: How A Family's Leap Of Faith Helped Lead Hank Brown To Iowa
articles.summary: From SEC castoff to Iowa’s unlikely hero, Hank Brown’s journey to the Hawkeyes’ upset of Michigan is a story of faith, perseverance and a family’s belief.
body: Tucked high in the upper rungs of Michigan Stadium, Eric Brown clasped his hands near his mouth, almost as if to warm them on a cool fall afternoon.
His wife, Lesley, stood to his right with the same pose – equally nervous, hands held equally tight, heart palpitations running equally high.

The Browns are deeply religious people. Sundays are spent at All Christ Church Nashville before plopping on the couch to watch NFL games or bouncing between any of their five children’s athletic events. They believe firmly in Christ. God has a path for all, they might tell you.

As Hank Brown’s eyes slid from center to left and the shotgun snap hit his hands, Eric and Lesley’s son cocked back the arm that was once deemed not good enough to carry Auburn back to relevancy and rifled a pass to the front left pylon of the end zone below his parents.
